distinguishing_features: Replaces active agitation with passive, static flow geometry (baffles) to maintain particle suspension
Uses existing hydraulic energy without any moving parts or external power input
Generates micro-turbulence and inertial recirculation via fixed internal structures in the delivery tube
Eliminates heat generation and mechanical wear associated with active stirring systems
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to prevent slurry particle settling in a CMP delivery system without introducing moving parts, additional energy input, or heat that could affect process stability
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism leverages well-understood fluid dynamics (Stokes' law, Dean vortices) and operates within feasible flow parameters using standard materials and geometries.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: While prior art uses active modulation of existing agitators, the shift to a fully passive, static turbulence-generating geometry that achieves suspension without any control system or moving part is not an obvious extension of active shear modulation.
